slug: 2026-01-26 The cost of Uganda's internet shutdown

facts.fact: The Uganda Communications Commission ordered the internet shut down nationwide on the evening of 13 January 2026, two days before the presidential election; the blackout lasted four days and access was restored a day after the Electoral Commission declared the winner, though State House, Parliament, security services, banks and hospitals stayed online.

After the internet was restored, social media and messaging apps stayed blocked, reachable only by VPN more than a week later, and the UCC Executive Director said they remained restricted to safeguard public order; date is the article's published date, 2026-01-26.

The Uganda Law Society condemned the UCC's internet shutdown, its vice president saying no state of emergency had been declared so the order was illegal, null, void and unconstitutional; the statement is undated, so the article's published date is used.
The president of the Uganda Medical Association wrote on 22 January 2026 that the internet and mobile money disruptions had created significant obstacles for the medical community.

systems.tiers: national; applied through MTN Uganda and Airtel Uganda

note: A lawsuit by two lawyers against UCC, the operators and the Attorney General is filed but undecided, so no barred fact.
